title: Strength of welded joints
intro:
The tensile strength X of a welded joint is normal with mean **420 MPa** and variance **225 MPa²**: X ~ N(420, 225).

Find the z-score of **400 MPa**, the probability that a joint is **weaker than 400 MPa**, the probability that its strength is **between 400 and 440 MPa**, and the strength that **99 % of joints exceed** (the 1st percentile). Give z and the probabilities to three decimals or more, and the strength to one decimal.

ZScore.says: You divided by 225, the variance. z divides by the standard deviation, σ = √225.

AtMost.says: You used 225 as σ. N(420, 225) gives the variance; the standard deviation is √225.
That is the area to the right of 400, P(X > 400). "Weaker than 400" is the area to the left: Φ(z).

Between.says: You used 225 as σ. N(420, 225) gives the variance; the standard deviation is √225.

Quantile.says: That is the 99th percentile, the strength 99 % of joints are below. You need the strength 99 % are above: the 1st percentile, μ − 2.326σ.

hints: N(μ, σ²) gives the variance. σ = √225 = 15 MPa.
z = (x − μ)/σ. P(X < 400) = Φ(z), from a table, stats.norm.cdf or pnorm.
Between is Φ(z₂) − Φ(z₁). The 1st percentile is μ + z·σ with Φ(z) = 0.01, so z = −2.326.
